721-complementary-courses-26-credits: At least 9 at 300+: Living World 3–15, Earth and Space 3–18, Environment 3–18, Material World 0–15, Technological World 3–12.
722-the-material-world: Up to 15 credits; the full 15 if you plan to teach Grade 11 Chemistry or Physics.
722-foundation-program: 30 credits: introductions in a teachable subject and other fields, maybe a First Year Seminar, with your adviser. Some History, Geography and Religious Studies can count toward the program. FRSL needs placement tests.
723-history-and-citizenship-culture-and-: 42 credits with your adviser. 24 History, 9 at 300–400: 3–9 European, 3–9 Asian, African, American, Latin American or Ancient, 6 on themes like social and gender history, culture, politics, conflict, wealth and science. 6–12 from the list, at least 3 each ECON and POLI.
724-culture-and-citizenship-in-quebec: Up to 9, at most 3 per subsection; others with an adviser.
726-history-and-citizenship-24-credits: 9 at 300–400: 3–9 European, 3–9 world or Ancient, 6 thematic. 6–12 from the list, at least 3 each ECON and POLI.
726-geography: 18 credits, or courses from the B.A. Geography minor with your adviser.
727-program-description: 120 credits (150 with Foundation) to certification. Language and language learning with field experience, for elementary and secondary ESL, adult ESL and Hellenic schools. A semester in Greece is encouraged. Build a professional portfolio.
727-additional-entrance-and-language-req: Pass the English Language Proficiency Test and a Greek test before admission; you're emailed how to register.
727-foundation-program: 30 credits with your adviser, including other languages. In Québec, ESL is taught in the French system, so French helps in placements and is required for jobs. FRSL needs placement tests.
727-required-courses-90-credits: One course runs every third year, alternating with CLAS 333 and 335. At least one Field Experience in a Hellenic school.
728-complementary-courses-30-credits: 3 each from three lists; 3 of FRSL or listed French by your level.
730-complementary-courses-24-credits: 3 each from three lists; 3 of FRSL or listed French by your level; 6–9 ENGL; 3–6 others, including up to 6 of foreign language.
731-programs-for-first-nations-and-inuit: OFNIE, under DISE, works with education authorities in Québec and Labrador (Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, Cree School Board, Kahnawake, Kanehsatake, Naskapi, Gesgapegiag, and Innu) to deliver community-based teacher education.
731-in-community-programs-for-first-nati: Certification and professional development without leaving your community.
731-admission-requirements-for-the-b-ed-: The Certificate in Education for First Nations and Inuit or equivalent, and your education authority's support. McGill decides.
731-admission-to-the-certificate-in-educ: Kativik applicants must be fluent and literate in Inuktitut or Inuinnaqtun; other languages are an asset. Normally a teacher or assistant with authorization and recommendations, aged 21+, or younger with Grade 12 or a DCS. McGill decides.
731-admission-requirements-for-the-certi: Fluent in the language of instruction, in a student adviser post in an Indigenous community, recommended locally, 21+ (admitted as a mature student). McGill decides.
732-admission-to-the-certificate-in-midd: Normally with or finishing the B.Ed. for Certified Teachers, ideally with two Indigenous language courses, recommended by your board. McGill decides.
732-admission-to-the-certificate-in-firs: Recommended by your community, 21+ or Secondary V, fluent in the language of instruction. Nunavik applicants need experience there. McGill decides.
732-admission-to-the-certificate-in-indi: Recommended by your community, 21+ or Secondary V. For professional development, Indigenous teachers in local schools. McGill decides.
732-program-description: For certified elementary teachers, 90 credits with at least 60 here and 30 transferable from listed certificates. After the 60-credit Certificate, 120 in total. Several certificates can be taken alongside. No further certification.
732-academic-concentration-30-credits: Five elementary subjects in a 12-9-3-3-3 pattern, or three in 15-9-6: arts, English, French, science, math, PE, moral and religious education, social studies, technology, or an Indigenous language.
732-program-description-2: Part-time in communities across Québec, for Algonquin, Cree, Inuit, Mi'gmaq, Mohawk and Naskapi people to become teachers, with Québec certification for Indigenous elementary schools. Then you can apply to a B.Ed.
733-time-limit: 12 years. After a long break, McGill may ask you to retake courses after five years.
733-naskapi: 27 credits from one stream: Generalist, Physical Education, or Culture and Language, with your adviser.
734-program-description: For Indigenous school personnel advisers: the principles of personnel services adapted to students' culture and needs, personal skills, community leadership, and shared knowledge. Qualifies you to work for an Indigenous education authority.
735-complementary-courses-9-credits: From the list or with approval. Courses from other departments depend on availability; the Adviser will arrange what's possible.
735-program-description: For established bilingual Indigenous teachers: teaching middle school suitably, adolescents' needs and the move to high school. No provincial certification. May fit within the B.Ed. for Certified Teachers.
735-education-courses-3-credits: From the list or approved by the Director.
735-program-description-2: Core leadership skills, reflective leaders partnering with parents, child development, community and cultural values in schools, and system understanding.
736-complementary-courses-12-credits: From the list or approved by the Director.
736-program-description: For Algonquin, Cree, Inuit, Mi'kmaq and Kanienkehaka students, mainly those teaching their language, with a focus on writing. May fit within the B.Ed.
736-language-courses: 6 credits: a beginning and a second-level course in the same language, such as EDEC 241 and 242.
737-program-description: For teachers and educators adapting curriculum to varied abilities and needs, in regular classrooms and in collaboration with other professionals.
737-complementary-courses-6-credits: Others with the Director's approval. Not always offered; check Minerva.
738-about-the-department-of-kinesiology-: B.Ed. in Physical and Health Education, B.Sc. Kinesiology Major or Honours, a Minor for Science, and M.A., M.Sc. and Ph.D.
738-location: Currie Gymnasium, 475 Pine Ave. W., 2nd Floor.
738-program-description: 120 credits (150 with Foundation) to certification, for elementary and secondary. Academics, professional work and teaching are interwoven, with responsibility growing early and steadily.
738-foundation-program: 30 introductory credits needed before U1. For a second subject, consider History, Geography, English or Math. Includes the 0-credit EDEC 215.
739-electives-12-credits: Any McGill courses, watching restrictions and prerequisites.
739-program-description: 90 credits (120 with Foundation): human movement from social, historical, psychological and biological angles, with room for minors. Honours needs CGPA 3.3 after two years, kept to graduation.
739-graduation-requirement: First Aid and CPR Level C, or equivalents, before graduating.
739-foundation-program: 29–30 credits of basic science, or equivalents from CEGEP. Fall and Winter BIOL and CHEM, plus MATH and PHYS chosen with an adviser.
